relevance.rationale: Genuine orphan. It rewrites the WDVV associativity equations as functional relations between second derivatives of a single prepotential F, analogous to the dispersionless Hirota equations, and discusses their properties — with the motivating class being prepotentials from low-energy effective actions of four-dimensional N=2 supersymmetric gauge theories via Seiberg-Witten theory. The folio does have Seiberg-Witten content (prop:mi-sw-abelianisation, prop:sw-period-residue-sum, prop:jet-sw-tau-decomposition), which is why this is tangential rather than not-relevant. But grep across content/, docs/ and computations/ returns ZERO hits for 'WDVV' and zero for 'prepotential' or 'special Kaehler': the folio uses the SW DIFFERENTIAL and its periods as a jet decomposition of the archimedean realisation, and never forms a prepotential F(a) or asks about associativity of a Frobenius-manifold structure. With no prepotential in the corpus there is nothing for the WDVV relations to constrain. Scope-(a): as read, this supplies nothing the folio can currently consume; if a prepotential is ever constructed from the folio's SW periods, it would become relevant immediately. Note for the bibliography: an author of this paper is already registered in the corpus for unrelated work on the folio's genus-4 curve, so name-matching alone should not be used to resolve this document.

proposedActions.rationale: The folio has SW differentials and periods but no prepotential and no Frobenius-manifold/associativity claim, so there is no target for the WDVV relations. Revisit if a prepotential is ever formed from prop:sw-period-residue-sum.
